title: One Pretrained Decision Model Is Enough for Training-Free Generalist Graph Anomaly Detection
abstract: arXiv:2610.30777v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Graph anomaly detection (GAD) aims to identify irregular entities in graph-structured data, yet heterogeneous anomaly patterns and distributional differences across graphs challenge generalizable detection. Existing training-free approaches avoid task-specific optimization but primarily rely on predefined numerical scoring rules, leaving the semantic interpretation of heterogeneous anomaly evidence largely unexplored. In this paper, we propose Jev-GAD, a training-free generalist graph anomaly detection framework that bridges heterogeneous numerical evidence and pretrained decision mechanisms. To address heterogeneous anomaly patterns, we construct complementary structural, attribute, and neighborhood evidence and transform heterogeneous statistics into graph-relative anomaly percentiles. To move beyond predefined numerical scoring rules, we leverage a single frozen pretrained language model for evidence-conditioned anomaly assessment. To

translated_title: 一个预训练决策模型足以实现免训练的通才图异常检测
translated_abstract: 图异常检测（GAD）旨在识别图结构数据中的不规则实体，然而异构的异常模式以及不同图之间的分布差异对可泛化的检测构成了挑战。现有的免训练方法虽然避免了特定任务的优化，但主要依赖于预定义的数值评分规则，使得对异构异常证据的语义解释在很大程度上尚未被探索。在本文中，我们提出了Jev-GAD，一个连接异构数值证据与预训练决策机制的免训练通才图异常检测框架。为了应对异构的异常模式，我们构建了互补的结构、属性和邻域证据，并将异构统计量转换为图相对异常百分位数。为了超越预定义的数值评分规则，我们利用单个冻结的预训练语言模型进行基于证据的异常评估。
tldr: Jev-GAD是一个免训练的通才图异常检测框架，通过将结构、属性和邻域等异构数值证据转化为图相对异常百分位数，并利用单个冻结的预训练语言模型进行基于证据的异常评估，实现了跨图的可泛化异常检测。
en_tdlr: Jev-GAD is a training-free generalist graph anomaly detection framework that transforms heterogeneous structural, attribute, and neighborhood evidence into graph-relative anomaly percentiles and leverages a single frozen pretrained language model for evidence-conditioned anomaly assessment, enabling generalizable anomaly detection across graphs.
